title: Sensorimotor alpha and beta ECoG during movement imagery (Stolk et al. 2019, shared participants S4-S6)
description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from three epilepsy patients (S4-S6) implanted with subdural grids and strips, acquired while they imagined grasping a cylinder with the left or right hand. The dataset is the subset of participants from Stolk et al. (2019) who consented to data sharing, released as trial segments. It supports investigation of alpha and beta rhythmic activity in human sensorimotor cortex during movement imagery.
methods_description: Recordings used a 128-channel Micromed system (22 bits, analog band-pass 0.15-134.4 Hz, 512 Hz sampling) with Ad-Tech subdural grids and strips (10 mm spacing, 2.3 mm exposed diameter). Patients performed a movement imagery task of 60 trials per session. Epochs with overt movements or distracting events were excluded by the authors. Trial segments are stored back-to-back in BrainVision files without filtering, re-referencing, or resampling.
